items.q: Which demographic profile belongs to PIGN/IRGN (infection-related GN) rather than to PSGN?
opts: Immunodeficient child, male > female, predisposed by diabetes mellitus
Immunocompetent child, male > female, aged 2–7 years
Immunocompetent school child presenting after a streptococcal sore throat
Healthy adolescent presenting after a GABHS skin infection
items.exp: The TYPES table contrasts the two entities: PIGN/IRGN arises in the immunodeficient child (male > female) with diabetes mellitus as the predisposing factor, whereas PSGN arises in the immunocompetent child. (Book p775)

items.q: A 5-year-old immunocompetent boy, previously healthy, develops cola-coloured urine and hypertension 10 days after a sore throat, with a low C3. Which table entry does he fit?
opts: PSGN — the commonest presentation is acute proliferative GN
PIGN/IRGN — the commonest presentation is RPGN
Thin basement membrane disease with persistent microhaematuria
items.exp: PSGN = immunocompetent child, age 2–7 years, streptococcal sore throat preceding by 7–10 days, presenting as acute proliferative glomerulonephritis with low C3. (Book p775)

items.q: PSGN follows infection with group A beta-haemolytic streptococci; as printed in the table, sore throat < skin infection as the predisposing infection.
opts: True — skin infection is the commoner predisposing infection
False — sore throat is the commoner predisposing infection
items.exp: The table's inequality 'sore throat < skin infection' means skin infection is the commoner predisposing streptococcal infection in PSGN — consistent with anti-DNAase B (a skin-infection antibody) being the marker used. (Book p775)

items.q: In the TYPES table, the PSGN age band is:
items.exp: PSGN demographic row: immunocompetent child, male > female, age 2–7 years. (Book p775)

items.q: Match the GABHS strain group with the infection it causes in PSGN — 1) Strains 1, 3, 4, 12  2) Strains 47, 49, 55, 57 … A) Sore throat (pharyngitis)  B) Skin infection
items.exp: Nephritogenic GABHS strains 1, 3, 4 and 12 cause sore throat, while strains 47, 49, 55 and 57 cause skin infection. (Book p775)

items.q: All but one of these GABHS strains are listed against skin infection in PSGN. Which strain is the odd one out?
items.exp: Strain 12 belongs to the pharyngitis group (1, 3, 4, 12); strains 47, 49, 55 and 57 are the skin-infection strains. (Book p775)

items.q: The organism responsible for PIGN/IRGN in the TYPES table is:
items.exp: PIGN/IRGN is caused by MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus), typically in an immunodeficient diabetic child. (Book p775)

items.q: Fill up: In PIGN/IRGN the commonest predisposing infection in a diabetic child is diabetic ______.
items.exp: Predisposing factors for PIGN/IRGN: diabetes mellitus, with diabetic foot/cellulitis as the commonest infection. (Book p775)

items.q: Match the incubation period with the triggering event — 1) Sore throat  2) Skin infection  3) PIGN/IRGN … A) Alongside the infection (no incubation period)  B) 7–10 days  C) 2–4 weeks
items.exp: PSGN incubation is 7–10 days after sore throat and 2–4 weeks after skin infection; PIGN/IRGN arises alongside the infection, with no incubation period. (Book p775)

items.q: PIGN/IRGN characteristically appears 2–4 weeks after the predisposing staphylococcal infection.
opts: False — it appears alongside the infection, with no incubation period
True — the incubation period is 2–4 weeks
True, but only when the skin is the portal of entry
False — it appears 7–10 days after the infection
items.exp: The incubation-period row reads 'alongside infection (no IP)' for PIGN/IRGN; the 2–4 week interval applies to PSGN after skin infection. (Book p775)

items.q: In the TYPES table, PSGN presents with a low C3 in what percentage of patients?
items.exp: PSGN presentation row: acute proliferative GN (commonest) with ↓C3 in 90% of patients. (Book p775)

items.q: An immunodeficient diabetic man with an infected foot develops rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis with a raised C3. The table's prognostic entry for this entity is:
opts: Good prognosis with no risk of CKD
items.exp: PIGN/IRGN presents as RPGN with ↑C3 in 60% and carries a poor prognosis, whereas PSGN has a good prognosis with no risk of CKD. (Book p775)

items.q: Match each entity with its table entry — 1) PSGN  2) PIGN/IRGN … A) Exudative proliferative GN with ↓C3 in 90%  B) RPGN with ↑C3 in 60%
items.exp: PSGN: acute proliferative GN, ↓C3 in 90%, good prognosis. PIGN/IRGN: RPGN, ↑C3 in 60%, poor prognosis. (Book p775)
